html:
The capture and plunder of Delhi by the Central Asian conqueror Timur in December 1398, after he defeated the army of the Delhi Sultanate outside the city.

The sultanate, under the weak Tughlaq ruler Nasir-ud-Din Mahmud Shah, was already divided. Timur crossed the Indus in the autumn and before the battle had a vast number of Indian prisoners killed, fearing they would rise against him. The sultan's war elephants could not save the day. After the city surrendered, fighting between soldiers and townsfolk turned into days of massacre and looting.

Timur stayed only a short time. He took huge booty and many skilled craftsmen back to Samarkand to build his capital. Delhi took a century to recover, and the sultanate broke into regional kingdoms. The raid left one long legacy: Timur's descendant Babur later claimed northern India as his heritage and in 1526 founded the Mughal Empire.
sum: The capture and plunder of Delhi by the Central Asian conqueror Timur in December 1398, after he defeated the army of the Delhi Sultanate outside the city.
